zones.label: Structured data (JSON-LD)
zones.text:
How is this different from Jellyfish or the dashboard we already have?
Your dashboard shows velocity and cycle time. It doesn't show what a feature costs in dollars, and it doesn't send anyone to fix what it found. The AI Intelligence Layer joins your AI spend to your actual work: every model call resolves to the person, feature, and model that produced it. Keep your dashboard, it won't argue with ours.
How do I know it works on our stack?
That's the Benchmark. One week, your environment, connected to your Jira and GitHub. You see your real numbers before committing to anything, and the baseline is yours whatever you decide.
Does our code or telemetry leave our environment?
No. The full pipeline deploys into your VPC: collector, queue, warehouse, dashboards. Telemetry never leaves the account, every figure resolves to a trace ID you can audit, and access is IAM-scoped with SSO and RBAC.
What counts as a shipped feature?
Features from your own backlog, graded by complexity, passing your quality gates. The AI Intelligence Layer prices them in dollars and compares like with like: what a medium feature costs you now versus three months ago. Your definitions, your data.
Will developers see this as surveillance?
The AI Intelligence Layer prices work, not people watching. Every developer sees their own numbers against the team average, managers see teams, execs see the org: RBAC by design. The conversation shifts from "who's slow" to "which tasks burn money on the wrong model," and that's a conversation engineers want to have.
How long until we see numbers?
First numbers in one week: the collector connects to Jira, GitHub, and your AI tools, and historical backfill starts pricing your recent work immediately. A full baseline builds over the first month.
What is AI cost management?
AI cost management means tracking, forecasting, attributing, and optimizing AI spend across models, tools, teams, and workflows. For GoGloby the key metric is cost per shipped feature, so every dollar ties to the engineering output it produced, measured against your own baseline.
How is AI cost management different from cloud cost management?
Cloud FinOps tracks infrastructure and cloud services. AI engineering cost management also needs model calls, tokens, prompts, AI coding sessions, PRs, CI runs, stories, and shipped features, none of which show up on a cloud bill.
What are AI cost management tools?
AI cost management tools track model spend, cloud AI costs, token usage, budget alerts, and allocation. GoGloby differs by joining AI spend to engineering output and forward-deploying engineers to fix what the AI Intelligence Layer finds, rather than only reporting the bill.
Who needs AI cost management software?
CTOs, VPs of Engineering, platform leaders, and finance leaders at companies with growing Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, OpenAI, Gemini, or Bedrock usage, and no clear connection between what they spend and what they shipped.
What happens after the Benchmark?
GoGloby establishes your baseline, then forward-deployed engineers work inside your team to reduce waste, set up the Agentic SDLC, and improve ROI month over month against that baseline. If you stop after the Benchmark, the baseline is yours to keep.

zones.label: How we work: What Is AI Cost Management?
zones.text:
What Is AI Cost Management?
AI cost management is the practice of tracking, attributing, forecasting, and optimizing AI spend across models, tools, teams, and workflows, tied to the engineering output it produced.
For GoGloby, the unit that matters is cost per shipped feature. The AI Intelligence Layer joins your AI spend to your actual work, so every dollar is attributed to a story, PR, model call, team, and the shipped feature it supported.
AI Cost Management vs. Cloud FinOps
Cloud FinOps tracks infrastructure and cloud services. AI cost management also has to see model calls, tokens, prompts, AI coding sessions, PRs, CI runs, stories, and shipped features, none of which appear on a cloud bill.
AI Cost Management vs. Engineering Dashboards
Engineering dashboards report velocity and cycle time, which are activity, not cost. AI cost management prices the work in dollars and ties it to what actually shipped.

zones.label: Company: Why AI Cost Management Breaks Inside Engineering Teams
zones.text:
THE PROBLEM
Why AI Cost Management Breaks Inside Engineering Teams
Agentic Output Is Measured. Its Cost Isn’t.
AI Spend Is Untraceable at Source
LLM invoices aggregate at the org level. Token usage inside Claude Code, Cursor, and Copilot sessions is never joined to the commits, PRs, or features it produced.
No Join Key From Feature to Model Calls
Jira and Linear track points and cycle time but never see tokens. Without session-to-feature attribution, cost per shipped feature is not a computable metric.
Model Mix Is Unmanaged
Expensive models routinely execute tasks a cheaper model could handle. With a large unit-price gap between model tiers and no per-task telemetry, routing waste is structurally invisible.
AI Cost Anomalies Surface Too Late
Retry loops, cache misses, and long-context blowups appear as line items 30 days later, not as same-day signals with a trace ID attached.

zones.label: Featured tiles: AI Cost Management Metrics Engineering Leaders Track
zones.text:
WHAT IT SHOW
AI Cost Management Metrics Engineering Leaders Track
What Engineering Leaders Measure, Sprint by Sprint
Cost Per Shipped Story
Ties the full AI cost of each completed story, from model calls to the PRs that closed it, back to the story itself. This is your core unit of value, the number that makes AI spend comparable across teams and sprints.
AI-Authored PR Rework
Tracks how much AI-generated code gets reopened, reverted, or rewritten after it first merges. High rework means you are paying twice for the same feature and shows where AI output is not yet production-ready.
Model Mix
Shows which models ran which tasks and what each tier cost against the work it produced. Expensive models routinely handle jobs a cheaper tier could do, and seeing the mix per task is how you catch that routing waste early.
Plan Versus Actual Spend
Compares forecasted AI spend to what each team actually consumed, sprint by sprint. It closes the gap between the budget you committed and the invoice you receive, and gives you next quarter’s number before you commit it.
Cost Per Merged PR
Attributes AI cost to every pull request that reaches main. It prices real engineering output at the PR level, so you can see which teams and workflows turn AI spend into shipped code most efficiently.
Failed CI Cost
Captures the AI and compute spend burned on pipeline runs that never passed. Failed CI produces nothing shippable, so tracking it surfaces the retry loops and flaky tests that quietly inflate your bill.

HOW WE DEPLOY IT
Governance Model for AI Cost Management Tools
Configuration splits between servers you control and MDM-managed workstations — Claude Code, Copilot + VS Code, and Cursor.
Customer cloud — servers
Org-level settings — source of truth
Integrations, teams, roles, API keys, telemetry & retention policy.
OTLP collector + ingest API
Per-person tokens; auth at the edge, IAM-scoped (e.g. AWS ECS).
SQS → ETL → attribution → RDS warehouse
Replayable queues; RBAC on every mart.
Dashboards · forecasts · signals · query tool
Read-only serving layer; nothing writes back to repos
Developer workstations — mixed toolchain
!
Org-managed policy — highest precedence
Pushed via MDM (e.g. managed-settings.json, org policies): permissions, telemetry endpoints, allow-lists; not overridable locally.

zones.label: Accordion 1: FAQs
zones.text:
FAQs
How is this different from Jellyfish or the dashboard we already have?
Your dashboard shows velocity and cycle time. It doesn’t show what a feature costs in dollars, and it doesn’t send anyone to fix what it found. The AI Intelligence Layer joins your AI spend to your actual work: every model call resolves to the person, feature, and model that produced it. Keep your dashboard, it won’t argue with ours.
How do I know it works on our stack?
That’s the Benchmark. One week, your environment, connected to your Jira and GitHub. You see your real numbers before committing to anything, and the baseline is yours whatever you decide.
Does our code or telemetry leave our environment?
No. The full pipeline deploys into your VPC: collector, queue, warehouse, dashboards. Telemetry never leaves the account, every figure resolves to a trace ID you can audit, and access is IAM-scoped with SSO and RBAC.
What counts as a shipped feature?
Features from your own backlog, graded by complexity, passing your quality gates. The AI Intelligence Layer prices them in dollars and compares like with like: what a medium feature costs you now versus three months ago. Your definitions, your data.
Will developers see this as surveillance?
The AI Intelligence Layer prices work, not people watching. Every developer sees their own numbers against the team average, managers see teams, execs see the org: RBAC by design. The conversation shifts from “who’s slow” to “which tasks burn money on the wrong model,” and that’s a conversation engineers want to have.
How long until we see numbers?
First numbers in one week: the collector connects to Jira, GitHub, and your AI tools, and historical backfill starts pricing your recent work immediately. A full baseline builds over the first month.
What is AI cost management?
AI cost management means tracking, forecasting, attributing, and optimizing AI spend across models, tools, teams, and workflows. For GoGloby the key metric is cost per shipped feature, so every dollar ties to the engineering output it produced, measured against your own baseline.
How is AI cost management different from cloud cost management?
Cloud FinOps tracks infrastructure and cloud services. AI engineering cost management also needs model calls, tokens, prompts, AI coding sessions, PRs, CI runs, stories, and shipped features, none of which show up on a cloud bill.
What are AI cost management tools?
AI cost management tools track model spend, cloud AI costs, token usage, budget alerts, and allocation. GoGloby differs by joining AI spend to engineering output and forward-deploying engineers to fix what the AI Intelligence Layer finds, rather than only reporting the bill.
Who needs AI cost management software?
CTOs, VPs of Engineering, platform leaders, and finance leaders at companies with growing Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, OpenAI, Gemini, or Bedrock usage, and no clear connection between what they spend and what they shipped.
What happens after the Benchmark?
GoGloby establishes your baseline, then forward-deployed engineers work inside your team to reduce waste, set up the Agentic SDLC, and improve ROI month over month against that baseline. If you stop after the Benchmark, the baseline is yours to keep.
